R01.note: Explains the lost recovery action and its measured timing, corrects the earlier recommendation, and explicitly acknowledges why it cannot provide authentic code.

errors: "the only real downside is slower rollback" claims an exhaustive assessment the evidence does not establish.
"checkout stays broken for roughly 12 minutes instead of 1" assumes complete checkout failure, successful mitigation, and no preparation time.
"How likely that is: low" assigns a likelihood unsupported by the incident history alone.
"Every change to checkout from here on goes untested against the legacy path" contradicts the continued presence of 31 legacy tests and invents future testing behavior.
"that untested code" mischaracterizes the legacy path, which has a dedicated test suite.
R02.note: The useful timing comparison is undermined by invented testing behavior and unjustified confidence about future incidents.

errors: "the only real downside" claims completeness beyond the supplied evidence.
"rollback goes from a ~1-minute flag flip to a ~12-minute deploy" compresses merge-to-live timing into total recovery timing and assumes the deploy mitigates the incident.
R03.note: Gives a compact, actionable comparison but omits the recovery sequence and the limits of the 12-minute measurement.

errors: "your only mitigation for a checkout incident becomes a redeploy" is not established for every incident.
"roughly a 10x slower time-to-mitigate" treats deployment duration as complete mitigation time.
"every minute costs conversions" invents a business impact not measured in the supplied facts.
"LaunchDarkly serving (trivial)" assigns an unverified cost judgment.
"the flag isn't protecting you from anything new" is unsupported.
"until the new flow has been through a real checkout incident or a high-traffic event" introduces an unsupported replacement for the agreed removal condition.

"Delete the legacy tests and the dead branch ... keep the flag as a kill-switch wired to a fail-safe" proposes an unspecified recovery mechanism after removing the branch that provides the verified fallback.
R04.note: Replaces the established cleanup condition with an invented waiting period and an incoherent partial cleanup.

errors: "The one real downside" claims an exhaustive assessment.
"Someone opens a revert of the removal PR ... The deploy runs" does not establish how restoring a flag still served at 100% actually switches customers to the legacy path.
"I only checked src/flags.ts and the storefront code paths" invents the precise scope of earlier inspection.
"say it isn't" treats meeting the cleanup condition as proof that the fast fallback has no remaining value.
R05.note: Provides useful named paths and preparation-time caveats, but repeats itself and leaves its proposed recovery sequence incomplete.

errors: "mitigate a checkout incident instantly" contradicts the measured approximately one-minute mitigations.
"merges the fix to main" invents the repository's canonical branch.
"The incident is mitigated when the deploy finishes" assumes the chosen revert fixes the incident.
"The LaunchDarkly audit log shows ... zero checkout incidents" attributes incident evidence to the flag audit log rather than the incident log.
"a 12-minute rollback time" treats merge-to-live duration as total rollback time.
R06.note: Corrects the earlier dismissal of CI cost, but presents a hypothetical recovery as guaranteed and misattributes its evidence.

errors: "a rollback deploy would take about 12 minutes" extends the measured production deployment timing to an unverified rollback procedure without stating the merge-to-live boundary.
R07.note: Answers directly and efficiently, but leaves the cleanup criteria, code locations, and recovery timing boundary for the reader to infer.

errors: "Violates issue #882" turns a removal eligibility condition into a proven violation.
"requires removal after 2 weeks" overstates the issue's stated condition.
The file links invent storefront source locations inside the judge's evaluation workspace.
"a 12-minute production deploy" omits that the measurement starts at merge and does not include preparing recovery.
R08.note: The short cost comparison is weakened by fabricated file targets and treating an issue's cleanup condition as a rule violation.

errors: "a checkout bug would take about 12 minutes to undo" initially presents merge-to-live duration as total recovery time.
"Checkout stays broken for that whole time" assumes the incident's severity and persistence.
"Someone reverts the deletion commit ... Checkout stays broken ..." omits the flag-off action needed to select the restored legacy path.
"I only checked that it's reachable solely when the flag is off" invents the precise scope of earlier inspection.
"the flag only saves you the difference between a 1-minute and a roughly 12-minute undo" contradicts its own acknowledgment of additional PR, CI, and review time.
"#882's own criteria say it's now proven" overstates a cleanup threshold as proof of reliability.
R09.note: Names relevant evidence and admits some uncertainty, but its recovery arithmetic contradicts its own detailed sequence.

errors: "if checkout breaks ... it's fixed in about a minute" generalizes two successful mitigations to every checkout failure.
"the same fix means reverting the PR and deploying" does not establish that a revert restores working checkout or selects the legacy path.
"the worst case ... about 12 minutes of broken checkout" invents an upper bound and omits diagnosis, preparation, and merge time.
"The risk ... looks low" is an unsupported likelihood estimate.
"nobody has needed the fallback" infers absence of need from absence of toggles.
"code that no user can reach" ignores that users can reach the legacy path when the flag is switched off.
R10.note: Offers a clear cleanup action, but repeatedly converts historical observations into guarantees about future recovery.

errors: "a checkout bug cannot be undone without writing, merging, and shipping a fix" excludes unverified recovery alternatives.
"That is the whole downside" claims an exhaustive assessment.
"this is how both pre-rollout incidents arrived" invents that deployments introduced bugs in the new flow.
"Orders start failing at payment" invents the incidents' failure mode.
"Both September incidents" invents incident dates; the supplied window includes part of August.
"two incidents in the six weeks before 100%" changes the supplied one-month incident window.
"revisit at, say, 6–8 weeks with no checkout change" introduces an unsupported waiting condition.
R11.note: Its detailed incident story appears concrete because it invents events, then uses those inventions to justify extending the agreed waiting period.

errors: "I infer the only recovery left is merging a fix and deploying it" marks an inference but still excludes alternatives the evidence does not address.
"about 11 minutes longer" subtracts historical mitigation time from deployment duration without including diagnosis or preparation.
"it has not broken since 2026-09-15" overstates the absence of logged checkout incidents.
"set the threshold for accepting the slower rollback" attributes a specific rationale to the issue that its supplied body does not state.
R12.note: Explains the verified flag behavior and reverses the earlier recommendation, but repeats the same facts and overstates what the incident log and issue establish.
